report.summary: All four failures trace to two product bugs in app/main.py, both switched on by the BUGS env var (leak_books and year_off_by_one). Nothing in the repo or workflow sets BUGS, so first confirm what environment ran this job; if it was an intentionally seeded build, these failures are the expected findings, and if not, fix the app's list_books scoping and year validation before anything else.

causes.title: GET /api/books and the books page return every user's books
causes.explanation: With leak_books enabled, list_books ignores owner_id and returns all rows, so one user can see another user's books and a brand-new user's bookshelf is not empty. This breaks the privacy test directly and makes the empty-state UI test fail because other users' rows are rendered.
evidence: app/main.py:163-164: if "leak_books" in BUGS: rows = conn.execute("SELECT * FROM books ORDER BY id").fetchall()
app/main.py:166: the correct query filters by owner_id = ?
tests/api/test_books_api.py:41-42: other_ids = [b["id"] for b in other_api.list_books().json()]; assert book["id"] not in other_ids (failed with 2 not in [1, 2])

tests/ui/test_login_ui.py:14: expect(books.empty_state).to_be_visible() fails; the aria snapshot shows rows "Final title Someone 2001" and "From API-a09ceb99 Robot" belonging to other tests' users, and no empty-state element
causes.suggested_fix: Restore owner scoping in list_books (filter by owner_id for all callers), and make sure BUGS is not set in the environment that runs the regular suite.

causes.title: Books with next year's publication year are accepted
causes.explanation: With year_off_by_one enabled, validate_book allows max_year = this_year + 1, so a year one past the current year is saved (201) instead of rejected (422) and no error is shown in the UI. The tests are correct: the error message and the rule are both defined as the current year being the maximum.
evidence: app/main.py:94: max_year = this_year + 1 if "year_off_by_one" in BUGS else this_year
app/main.py:96: raise HTTPException(422, f"Year must be between 1 and {this_year}") is never reached for next year
tests/api/test_books_api.py:58 and 66: {"year": THIS_YEAR + 1} expects 422 but got "assert 201 == 422"
tests/ui/test_books_ui.py:44: expect(books.error).to_contain_text("Year must be between") fails with element(s) not found; the snapshot shows a row "Future-c4341a62 Someone 2027" was saved
causes.suggested_fix: Set max_year to this_year (remove the year_off_by_one seeded bug from the environment, or fix the comparison in app/main.py) so next-year input is rejected by both the API and the form.
